plain_text:
FITCHBURG PUBLIC LIBRARY
BOARD OF TRUSTEES
Minutes September 16, 2026
Trustees present: Chair Matthew Bruun, Sabrina Holley-Williams, Mary Rice Hurley, Joanne 
Huse, Cynthia Jones, Muna Kangsen, Eric Mbunwe, Daniel Spigelmyer, Jim Walsh, and Director 
Deb Hinkle
CALL TO ORDER at 6:30 P.M.
PUBLIC COMMENT: None
CAMPAIGN REPORT:  Rob Favini from the OWL Campaign attended.  He reported that the OWL 
Campaign has met its goal of 3.5 million dollars. Rob thanked his team as well as Deb Hinkle, 
Library Director.  The Legacy of Learning project has been successful, too.  There have been 
many tours and meetings with donors, and many grants were written by the Library Director.  
Many connections were made with schools, banks, and community organizations.
Jim Walsh suggested that Rob contact WGBH’s program on Gateway cities so they can cover the 
library’s renovation.
MINUTES:  June Minutes were approved after an amendment correcting two errors.
DIRECTOR’S REPORT:
 The State Aid reports have been completed.  Due to more staffing and other expenses 
for the new library, state aid will be used for materials.
 Parking has become difficult for both staff and patrons. Library employees have 10 
spaces in the parking garage across the street.  Director Hinkle would like to secure the 
spaces behind the Arc and to remove the parking meters.  The Mayor and city agencies 
are helping in the effort to increase parking, as well as designate spaces as “Library 
Parking Only”.
 One part-time library employee has left for a position with more hours.  The position will
be posted by Human Resources.
 The Children’s Room HVAC is dripping due to condensation.  Parts of the collection 
affected have been moved. When the air conditioning is off, the condensation issue 
should improve.
 The “Freedom to Read” Act was signed this summer, and a pen from the signing was 
given to our library.  It is on display now.
 The Summer Reading Program was a success with 228 children, 35 teens, and 84 adults 
participating.
 Our new mascot has not gone public yet.  We need to vote on its name.  We looked at 
the nominations and decided unanimously on the name Wallace, who will walk on Main 
St. at the Halloween event on October 24th.
 All One Credit Union recently partnered with the children’s and teen departments to 
provide financial workshops.  
 The Parks and Recreation Department will provide afterschool and out-of-school 
programming with us through a $20,000 grant from the United Way.  The grant will
provide 3-5 hours of STEAM programming each week.  Our children’s and teen librarians
will run this programming in partnership with Parks and Recreation.
 The storytime program at Hollis Hills was quite popular and was covered on FATV.  It can
be found at FATV.org.
 The monthly budget was included in our packet.
 The Friends of the Library will participate in Saturday’s Food Truck Festival, holding up a 
pop-up book sale.
 The library participated in National Library Card Sign-up throughout the month of 
September. 
 Groton Hill offers free music lessons.  It was suggested that this could they be offered at 
the Library in the future.
TREASURER’S REPORT:  Joanne gave her last report as treasurer.  She reported that we still 
have funds in our accounts after the donation to the OWL Campaign.  Matt thanked her for her 
years of service.
BUILDING REPORT:  The opening of the new library building has been delayed until June due to 
construction delays and problems with the supply chain.  As a result, we will have to continue 
paying rent for the temporary space.  We will ask the city for a loan to pay our bills until we 
receive 1.4 million from the MBLC Escalation Payment.  Monies were allocated by the MBLC for 
all libraries under construction.  The City Council will meet at 6:00 P.M. Wed., Sept. 23rd, to 
discuss this request.  Trustees were encouraged to attend.
Both libraries will be closed for 4-6 weeks to complete the moves, training, etc.
POLICIES REPORT:  Nothing new.  We anticipate more policies will be necessary in our new 
space.
NOMINATIONSR REPORT:  The slate of officers was presented as follows:
President:  Matthew Bruun
Secretary:  Cynthia Jones
Treasurer:  Eric Mbunwe
The slate was voted in unanimously.
The meeting was adjourned at 7:50.
Respectfully submitted,
Cynthia Jones
Secretary
